clue.text: Rogue punched by husband in a state

indicators.note: being punched by something means having it driven into you, so H goes inside the word for rogue

parts.note: a cad is a rogue, a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A scoundrel gets thumped by a husband while in an agitated state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' looks like a description of the rogue's mood; 'a state' is the definition, the African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a landlocked country in north-central Africa, so it is a nation or state.

clue.text: Drug pipe with piece of resin inside

indicators.note: inside places the resin letter within the word for pipe

parts.note: a hose is a flexible pipe

indicators.note: a piece of the word resin is taken here as its first letter

explanation.surface: A drug user's pipe with a bit of cannabis resin in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse is slang for heroin, a narcotic.

clue.text: Choose to cover up one divine murder?

indicators.note: covering up something means enclosing it, so the word for choose wraps around the one

parts.note: to decide is to choose
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone opts to hush up a killing that seems heaven-sent.
explanation.definitionFit: Deicide is the killing of a god; 'divine murder' is that, with the question mark flagging the playful reading.

clue.text: One aboard ship will get more raunchy

indicators.note: aboard puts the one on board, inside the word for ship

parts.note: a steamer is a steamship
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A passenger on a ship expects things to get spicier.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy describes erotic, sexy content, so its comparative means sexier.

clue.text: Sides of swede coming with a main

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a swede is a root vegetable, here supplying its outer letters

explanation.surface: Swede served alongside a main course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like the main course; in crosswords 'the main' is the open ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic term for the open ocean, as in the Spanish Main.

clue.text: Nurse turned Hoskins around, primarily for this!

definitions.text: Nurse turned Hoskins around, primarily for this!

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse

indicators.note: turned means the word for the setter is read backwards

parts.note: the setter, Hoskins, refers to himself, so the setter gives ME

indicators.note: primarily takes only the first letter of around

explanation.surface: A nurse rolls the patient over, and we can guess what for.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a nurse turning the setter over is exactly the setting for this procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is a medical procedure for which a patient is usually turned onto their side.

clue.text: Huge mediums embracing a flapper going into the light

indicators.note: embracing means holding the a between the two letters

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for medium, as in clothing sizes, so two give MM
a moth is a fluttering insect drawn to light

explanation.surface: Psychics hug a fluttering 1920s girl heading towards the light, as in a seance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flapper' suggests a 1920s girl; here it is a moth, which flaps its wings toward a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth as an adjective means enormous, from the giant extinct elephant.

clue.text: Rolling reefer or downing drop of red? Perfect!

indicators.note: rolling means the letters are turned over and mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a drop of red is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A choice between rolling a joint or knocking back some red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix up REEFER, OR and R (the first letter of red), which is 'downed' along with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without a single mistake is flawless, so error-free means perfect.

clue.text: Coach and hot English bodyguard will have an affair

parts.note: a coach is a bus
IN means fashionable, i.e. hot
the SS was originally Hitler's bodyguard unit

explanation.surface: A coach and a trendy English minder are having a fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affair' suggests romance; it is used in the sense of a matter or concern.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair can mean a matter or concern, as in 'that's my business'.

clue.text: Possessing joints, a curate lit up

indicators.note: up here means stirred up or in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A curate gets high, holding several joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lit up' looks like smoking the joints; 'up' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Articulate in its anatomical sense means jointed, having segments connected by joints.

clue.text: Old red blemishes on the tongue?

indicators.note: on the tongue means as spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: marks are blemishes or spots

explanation.surface: Spots appearing on someone's tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Red is a nickname for a communist; Karl Marx is the original one.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Marx, the nineteenth-century founder of communism, is a long-dead communist.

clue.text: Sign half-redacted page with half-cut minister?

indicators.note: half of the word page is blacked out, leaving its second half

parts.note: taken as written, before half is removed

indicators.note: half of the word minister is cut away, leaving its first half

parts.note: taken as written, before half is cut

explanation.surface: Someone signs a partly blacked-out document alongside a tipsy minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' means drunk in British slang, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the Twins, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Having wavered, pay owner for guns etc.

indicators.note: having wavered means having gone back and forth, so the letters are shifted about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: After hesitating, someone pays the owner for firearms.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaponry is weapons collectively, covering guns and other arms.

clue.text: Networks hacked by a power Penny programs online

indicators.note: being hacked by means being broken into, so these letters go inside the word for networks

parts.note: webs are networks

explanation.surface: Computer networks are breached by a hacker named Penny with power.
explanation.definitionFit: Web apps are software applications run through a browser over the internet.

clue.text: Hamper that's opened by politician Balls?

indicators.note: opened by means split apart with these letters put in the gap

parts.note: i.e. stands for 'that is', so that's gives IE
MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician
Ed Balls is a former UK Labour politician, so Balls gives his first name ED

explanation.surface: A gift hamper being unwrapped by Ed Balls, the British politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls was a British Labour cabinet minister, so 'politician Balls' reads as two pieces, the job title and his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper is to hinder or obstruct, which is what impede means.

clue.text: Mom playing around with hooter in this?

definitions.text: Mom playing around with hooter in this?

indicators.note: playing around means fooling about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mom fooling about with a car horn on a road trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a vehicle in which Mom might toot the horn.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorhome is a large vehicle fitted out as living quarters, which has a horn to sound.

clue.text: Republican getting in troubles comrades

indicators.note: getting in means the R goes inside the word for troubles

parts.note: bothers is a verb meaning troubles

explanation.surface: A Republican politician runs into difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Brothers are fellow members of a movement or union, which is to say comrades.

clue.text: Unusually, hope a mod played in a brass band?

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Remarkably, a Sixties mod might be hoped to play in a brass band.
explanation.definitionFit: Oompah is the rhythmic bass sound of a tuba, so to oompah is to make that sound in a band.

clue.text: Staff happy about end of arduous projects?

parts.note: a stick is a staff

indicators.note: the end of arduous is its last letter

parts.note: up means happy, as in feeling up

explanation.surface: Office staff cheer at the conclusion of difficult projects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'projects' looks like a noun about work; it is the verb, to jut out.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick up is to protrude or jut out, which is to project.

clue.text: Cold cop annoyed with kit in driver's compartment

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: annoyed means stirred up or agitated, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chilly, irritated police officer sits in a car with his gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockpit is the enclosed space where a racing driver or pilot sits.

clue.text: King getting hug off brass? Cheeky blighter!

indicators.note: the king gets a hug from the brass, so the word for brass wraps around it

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: A monarch embraced by the top brass, a cheeky character.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass is British slang for money; a blighter is a rogue or rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey is an affectionate name for a mischievous child or rascal.

clue.text: Tyneside soldier upset that man had sounded like a nag?

parts.note: NE is North East England, where Tyneside lies

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the soldier is read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
he'd is the contraction of he had

explanation.surface: A Geordie soldier is upset that a man had been nagging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nag' looks like a scold; it is an old horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Neighing is the sound a horse makes, and a nag is a horse.

clue.text: Nutty biscuits

definitions.meaning: second meaning: thin crisp savoury biscuits

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests biscuits with nuts in; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is British slang for insane, and also the plural of a dry savoury wafer.

clue.text: Host of drugs Member of Congress will tuck into

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so the MC sits between the Es

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so a plural drugs here gives several Es
MC is the abbreviation for Member of Congress

explanation.surface: A congressman is about to tuck into a hoard of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host of' looks like 'lots of'; Host is the definition and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An emcee is a master of ceremonies, the presenter who hosts a show.

clue.text: Savage woman I'm always cuddling

indicators.note: cuddling means holding the answer within the run of words

explanation.surface: A wild woman says she is always hugging.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is a brutish, uncivilised person, just as a savage is.

clue.text: A jerk taking right in heavy goods vehicle

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the R goes inside the a plus the word for jerk

parts.note: a tic is a sudden involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: An idiot driving a lorry takes a right turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' suggests an idiot driver; it is a twitch. An artic is British for an articulated lorry, a large truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Artic is short for articulated lorry, a big truck in two hinged parts.

clue.text: Love to get stuck into drink … it's a liquid food!

indicators.note: getting stuck into means going inside, so the O goes into the word for drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: Someone who loves to get stuck into a drink claims it counts as food.
explanation.definitionFit: Soup is a dish made by cooking ingredients in stock, eaten as a liquid.

clue.text: Headwear cadet hocks after mobilisation

indicators.note: after mobilisation means once set in motion, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cadet pawns his kit after being called up.
explanation.walkthrough: To hock something is to pawn it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocked hats are three-cornered or bicorne hats worn historically by officers.

clue.text: Price finally cut for a leafy vegetable

indicators.note: finally cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: cost is price

explanation.surface: A price reduction at last for a leafy vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos is a variety of lettuce with long crisp leaves, also called romaine.

clue.text: Perhaps down drug administered to old men

indicators.note: administered to puts the drug into the old men, so E goes inside

parts.note: old man is slang for father, so old men gives fathers
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug is given to elderly men, perhaps to bring them down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like a mood; it is soft plumage, an example of feathers, hence 'Perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is the fine soft plumage of birds, one kind of feathers.

clue.text: Get down and dance at front with posh perfumier?

indicators.note: at front picks the first letter of dance

parts.note: U means upper-class, i.e. posh
CK is Calvin Klein, the fashion house known for perfume

explanation.surface: An invitation to get down and dance up front with a fancy scent maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get down' suggests dancing; it means to lower your head.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck is to crouch or bob down quickly to avoid something.
